chunks.heading: Variety
chunks.text: Available in dozens of colors, profiles, and performance levels, asphalt shingles let homeowners match any architectural style or neighborhood standard. From classic gray to weathered wood tones, there is a shingle for every home.

chunks.heading: Easy Repair
chunks.text: When hail or wind damages a section of shingle roof, individual shingles can be replaced without disturbing the surrounding roofing. This makes storm damage repairs faster and more affordable than with most other materials. For flat or low-slope sections, see our asphalt flat roof repair services in Amarillo .

chunks.heading: Proven Performance
chunks.text: Asphalt shingles have been the standard residential roofing material in Texas for decades. Manufacturers continually improve formulations for better UV resistance, impact performance, and wind uplift ratings specific to severe weather regions.

chunks.heading: Deck Preparation
chunks.text: After removing old shingles, we inspect the roof deck for rot, water damage, and structural integrity. Damaged decking is replaced with new plywood or OSB sheathing. The deck must be clean, dry, and structurally sound before any new materials go down. 2

chunks.heading: Starter Strip
chunks.text: Factory-adhesive starter strips are installed along eaves and rakes. These create the critical first seal that prevents wind uplift along the most vulnerable roof edges. Proper starter strip installation is essential for wind performance. 4

chunks.heading: Ridge Cap and Flashing
chunks.text: Ridge cap shingles are installed along all peaks for a finished appearance and weather seal. Metal flashing is installed around chimneys, vents, walls, and all penetration points. Pipe boots and vent collars are sealed to prevent water entry at every junction. 6

chunks.heading: Cleanup and Final Inspection
chunks.text: We run magnetic nail sweeps across the yard and driveway, bag all debris for disposal, and perform a final walkthrough with the homeowner. You receive warranty documentation and a completed installation report for your records.

chunks.heading: How Do You Repair and Maintain Asphalt Shingles?
chunks.text: Efficient repairs and regular maintenance keep your shingle roof performing for its full expected lifespan. Here are the most common maintenance tasks:

chunks.heading: Addressing Granule Loss
chunks.text: Granules protect the asphalt layer from UV damage. Excessive granule loss (visible as bare or dark patches on shingles) accelerates aging. While some granule shedding is normal in new shingles, significant loss on established roofs indicates it may be time to plan for replacement .

chunks.heading: Fixing Leaks
chunks.text: Leaks typically originate at flashing points, damaged pipe boots, or sections with missing shingles. We trace leaks to their source (which is often not directly above the water stain), repair the entry point, and verify the fix with water testing when conditions allow.

chunks.heading: Extending Lifespan
chunks.text: Annual roof inspections , prompt minor repairs, proper attic ventilation, and keeping gutters clear all contribute to maximizing your shingle roof's service life. These preventive measures cost far less than premature replacement.

chunks.heading: Hidden Wind Damage
chunks.text: • Sealant failure: High-wind stress breaks invisible adhesive bonds around flashing and penetrations—undetectable without professional inspection • Fastener withdrawal: Uplift forces gradually pull roofing nails from decking—compromises structural integrity before visible damage appears • Underlayment damage: Wind-driven debris penetrates felt paper through small tears—creates leak paths invisible from exterior inspection • Thermal movement: Wind-accelerated temperature cycling expands/contracts materials at different rates, creating microscopic separation gaps

chunks.heading: Coverage Basics
chunks.text: Most Texas homeowner policies include wind damage coverage under "windstorm and hail" provisions. However, coverage specifics vary significantly between carriers, especially regarding wind speed thresholds and deductible structures. State Farm: Named storm deductible vs. wind/hail deductible Allstate: Catastrophic loss provisions for widespread events USAA: Military families often have enhanced wind coverage Farmers: Percentage deductibles based on dwelling value
